rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The **triple point** of a substance is the unique temperature and pressure where solid, liquid and gas coexist in equilibrium — for water **273.16 K at 611.7 Pa**. On the P–T phase diagram the fusion, vaporization and sublimation curves meet there; below the triple pressure the liquid phase cannot exist, which is why dry ice sublimes (CO₂'s P_tp = 5.18×10⁵ Pa exceeds 1 atm) and why freeze-drying works.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - T_tp(water) = 273.16 K; P_tp = 611.7 Pa - Kelvin (pre-2019): 1 K = T_tp/273.16

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Triple point ≠ ice point:** 273.16 K at 611.7 Pa vs 273.15 K at 1 atm — close in temperature, worlds apart in pressure.  ·  **Below the triple pressure, liquid cannot exist** — solid sublimes straight to vapour.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not quote 0°C and 1 atm as the triple-point conditions.  ·  The definition applies to one pure substance in equilibrium.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Dry ice*** — 1 atm < P_tp(CO₂) = 5.18×10⁵ Pa → sublimation at −78.5 °C.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: No verified PYQ; NEB-style practice (definition + significance 2–3m).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Distinguish water’s triple point from its normal-pressure melting point.  ·  What changes when heat is supplied at the triple point while all phases coexist?

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "273.16 K, 611.7 Pa, three phases — and 'defines the kelvin'."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Short (2m): Why can liquid CO₂ not exist at 1 atm?** — 1 atm lies below CO₂'s triple-point pressure (5.18×10⁵ Pa); the liquid phase is thermodynamically unstable there, so solid sublimes directly to gas.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Quote both values; the significance (kelvin definition) carries the marks.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **One point, three phases, one kelvin:** the triple point is thermometry's reproducible foundation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Water triple point: 273.16 K, 611.7 Pa — solid+liquid+gas in equilibrium.  ·  It anchored the kelvin: T_tp ≡ 273.16 K exactly.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Freeze-drying of food and vaccines works below the triple pressure: ice sublimes without melting.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: At the triple point → A  ·  Water's triple point is → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Where Three Phases Meet At exactly 273.16 K and 611.7 Pa, water coexists as ice, liquid and vapour simultaneously — the triple point. It is not a laboratory curiosity: it *defines* the kelvin, anchoring every temperature measurement on Earth.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Definition The **triple point** of a substance is the unique temperature and pressure at which its **solid, liquid and gaseous phases coexist in equilibrium**. For water: $$T_{tp} = 273.16 \text{ K} \;(0.01\ °C), \qquad P_{tp} = 611.7 \text{ Pa} \;(0.006\ \text{atm})$$ ### 2.2 Phase diagram context On a P–T diagram the three phase-boundary…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 45:** fixed points calibrate thermometers; the triple point is the most reproducible one. - **To ideal gas (Unit 13):** the old kelvin definition used ideal-gas thermometry matched at the triple point. - **To latent heat:** at the triple point, all three latent heats can be exchanged simultaneously.
